title: Structural strength of 3D-printed regolith construction
bottleneck: Printing habitats from lunar or Martian regolith — by sintering, binders, or solar melting — could slash launched mass, but printed regolith is brittle, porous, and weak in tension; holding a pressurized atmosphere inside a printed structure demands strengths no printed-regolith sample has demonstrated at scale. Binders imported from Earth defeat the mass savings; alternative binders are experimental. Thermal cycling, micrometeorites, and radiation aging of printed structures are uncharacterized.
why_it_blocks: If printed regolith cannot hold pressure, it can only make unpressurized structures like berms and pads, and habitats must still be imported — halving the ISRU construction payoff.
current_state: ESA and NASA have printed small regolith structures and test walls. No pressurized printed-regolith structure has been built or tested, on Earth or off.
